errors: "That is the only practical difference" overstates the evidence about open and closed issues.
"The crash can no longer happen on a supported device" extends evidence about Android 9 installation to all supported devices.
"v3.2 is unblocked" assumes there are no other open issues in the milestone.
R01.note: Explains the release cost and corrects the blanket closure recommendation, but overstates what the verified facts establish.

errors: "Android 9 devices ... can't hit this crash" should be limited to current builds; older installed builds are not addressed.
"the open record that forces a fix" overstates the gate, which also permits a user-approved won't-fix decision.
R02.note: Gives actionable consequences for each issue, but repeats lengthy references and leaves the flash as a symptom rather than a reproduction sequence.

errors: "If we close all four, it ships" confuses removing these blockers with actually shipping and assumes no other milestone blockers.
"There's nothing left to fix in the current app" treats exclusion of Android 9 as proof that no relevant defect remains.
R03.note: Clearly retracts the earlier reasoning and separates completed work from unresolved bugs, but makes release and defect claims stronger than the evidence.

errors: "Closing them unblocks it" assumes these four are the only release blockers.
"#402, #403, and #404 ... are already resolved" incorrectly treats the Android 9 support change as resolution of the crash.
"Closing them is correct" includes closing #403 without the user's required won't-fix decision.
R04.note: Answers the immediate release consequence concisely, but substitutes an obsolete verdict for the required decision on the Android 9 crash.

errors: "Closing does three concrete things and nothing more" claims an exhaustive account without evidence.
"#403 — won't-fix by product decision" presents a disposition that the user has not yet decided.
R05.note: Explains retained history and the release gate, but bare issue and PR numbers force the reader to reconstruct the supporting facts.

errors: "closing it would ship v3.2" treats issue closure as a release action.
"Close: the release unblocks" for #402 and #404 ignores the other unresolved blockers.
"the tracker says it's resolved" ignores the distinction between completed and won't-fix closures.
"no build we ship can hit this crash" extends current-build installation evidence beyond its verified scope.
R06.note: Includes a useful flash reproduction and acknowledges unknown additional blockers, but repeatedly restates the gate and contradicts that uncertainty elsewhere.

errors: "If all four close ... v3.2 can ship" assumes no other open milestone issues.
"Nothing is left to fix" is not established by Android 9 being excluded from current builds.
"The gate clears" after closing #401 ignores the other open issues.
"nothing in the tracker records it" is false: closing an issue retains its record.
"Android 9 users ... can't hit the crash" does not account for older installed builds.
R07.note: Explains individual choices and marks its deadline inference, but falsely says closure erases the bug's record.

R08.note: Connects leaving issues open to the release gate, shows the flash reproduction, and distinguishes an installation restriction from a verified crash fix.

errors: "I will close #402, #403, and #404" violates the requirement that the user decide #403's won't-fix disposition.
"Closing them removes them from the milestone" is false: closing changes issue state, not milestone membership.
"so the release can ship" overlooks #401 remaining open and blocking release.
"closing #401 violates your standing rule" is too broad; user-approved won't-fix closure is permitted.
R09.note: Provides concrete gate and flash sequences, but its proposed action contradicts the user's rule and its account of milestone membership is wrong.

errors: "a reader opening #470 sees the corrected copy" claims specific PR contents not supplied in the verified facts.
"Because the crash was never fixed" is unverified; the facts establish only that current builds exclude Android 9.
"move it out of the v3.2 milestone instead of closing it" recommends bypassing the release gate while leaving a reproduced bug unresolved, contrary to the no-bug-backlog rule.
R10.note: Explains installation and startup events concretely, but excessive repetition culminates in a recommendation to defer the live bug.

errors: "It also records that the work is resolved or that you've decided not to fix it" treats closure itself as evidence of completion or a decision, although either needs supporting documentation.
R11.note: Answers directly and respects the user's authority, but omits the PR evidence, Android version restriction, and reproduction details needed to judge its recommendations.

errors: "that is the whole reason they are still open" invents an exclusive causal explanation from the absence of PR references.
"Android 9 users can't install the app and can't hit the crash" should be limited to current builds.
"whether the release gate ... only counts open issues" introduces uncertainty about the blocking rule already supplied as verified.
"it's also the only state that stops an issue from holding the v3.2 gate" ignores removal from the milestone.
"we no longer ship to that OS is your call to make" conflates the already-established support change with the still-required won't-fix decision.
R12.note: Separates the four outcomes usefully, but repeats the explanation and adds unsupported causal claims and contradictory uncertainty.
